chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus; and Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad Abu Saeed, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Ibn Muskan, from Abu Basir, who said:
I asked Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام) about the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic:
Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.

He said: It was revealed concerning Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (عليهم السلام). I said to him: The people say, why is it that He did not name Ali and the People of his Household (عليهم السلام) in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic? He said: Say to them: the salat (prayer) was revealed to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), yet Allah did not specify for them three or four, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them. And zakat (alms-tax) was revealed to him, yet He did not specify for them that from every forty dirhams there is one dirham, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them. And hajj (pilgrimage) was revealed, yet He did not say to them: perform tawaf seven times, until the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) was the one who explained that to them.
And this was revealed: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger and those vested with authority among you.

And it was revealed concerning Ali, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn. So the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) said concerning Ali: Whoever I am his mawla, then Ali is his mawla. And he (صلى الله عليه وآله) said: I enjoin you concerning the Book of Allah and my Ahl al-Bayt, for I asked Allah, Mighty and Majestic, not to separate between the two until they bring me to the Pond, and He granted me that. And he said: Do not teach them, for they are more knowledgeable than you. And he said: They will never bring you out from a gate of guidance, nor will they ever make you enter a gate of misguidance.
Indeed Allah only desires to remove defilement from you, O People of the House, and to purify you with a thorough purification.

Had the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) remained silent and not clarified who the People of his Household were, the family of so-and-so and the family of so-and-so would have claimed it. But Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed it in His Book as a confirmation of His Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله). So they were Ali, al-Hasan, al-Husayn, and Fatimah (عليهم السلام). The Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) gathered them under the cloak in the house of Umm Salamah, then said: O Allah, every Prophet has a family and a weighty trust, and these are the People of my Household and my weighty trust. Umm Salamah said: Am I not among your family? He said: You are upon goodness, but these are my family and my weighty trust.

When the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) passed away, Ali was the worthiest of the people over the people because of the abundance of what the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) had conveyed concerning him, his appointing him before the people, and his taking him by the hand. When Ali passed away, Ali neither could nor would place Muhammad ibn Ali, nor al-Abbas ibn Ali, nor any of his sons in that position, for then al-Hasan and al-Husayn could have said: Allah, Blessed and Exalted, revealed concerning us as He revealed concerning you; so He commanded obedience to us as He commanded obedience to you; and the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) conveyed concerning us as he conveyed concerning you; and He removed defilement from us as He removed it from you.
And those related by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.

When Ali (عليه السلام) passed away, al-Hasan (عليه السلام) was worthiest of it because of his seniority. Then when he passed away, he could not place it in his son, nor would he do that, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: And those related by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah. If he were to place it in his son, then al-Husayn would have said: Allah commanded obedience to me just as He commanded obedience to you and to your father; and the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) conveyed concerning me just as he conveyed concerning you and your father; and Allah removed defilement from me just as He removed it from you and from your father.
And those related by blood are nearer to one another in the Book of Allah.

When it came to al-Husayn (عليه السلام), no one from his Ahl al-Bayt could claim against him as he could claim against his brother and his father, had they wished to turn the matter away from him, though they would never have done so. Then when it came to al-Husayn (عليه السلام), the interpretation of this verse took effect. Then after al-Husayn it passed to Ali ibn al-Husayn, and after Ali ibn al-Husayn it passed to Muhammad ibn Ali (عليه السلام).

And he said: Defilement is doubt. By Allah, we never doubt concerning our Lord. Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Yahya ibn Imran al-Halabi, from Ayyub ibn al-Hurr and Imran ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abd Allah (عليه السلام), similarly to that.

key_terms.أَهْلَ الْبَيْتِ: the Prophet’s Household specifically identified in this narration
key_terms.أُولِي الْأَمْرِ: those vested with divinely mandated authority whose obedience is commanded
key_terms.الْحَوْضَ: the Pond to which the Book and Ahl al-Bayt are said to return together
key_terms.تَأْوِيلُ: the realized interpretation or unfolding application of a verse
key_terms.تَطْهِيرًا: complete purification granted by Allah to Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.ثِقْلِي: my weighty trust, referring to the entrusted legacy mentioned by the Prophet
key_terms.مَوْلَاهُ: one whose authority, guardianship, or mastership is affirmed

ai.seo_question: Who are the ones meant by ‘those vested with authority among you’ in Qur'an 4:59 according to al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the verse commanding obedience to those vested with authority refers to Ali ibn Abi Talib, al-Hasan, and al-Husayn (عليهم السلام), and that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) clarified their authority just as he explained the details of salat, zakat, and hajj that were not fully specified in the Qur'an. It further links this authority to the purification of Ahl al-Bayt and presents the succession of the Imamate through the designated members of the Prophet’s Household.
